title: Blackpool, Double Check Stomp and the films
summary: Braud recalls an English band in Blackpool in 1933, writing Double Check Stomp from Amos and Andy, and appearing in several films.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: What was that other one that you come through? You said, good on Saturday night.

Well, I went, I went, I went, I went, Copenhagen. No, I went Blackpool in 1933. And I was playing on one side of the hall, and it was an English band playing on another, on the other side of the hall. So, he come in and asked me what kind of tuba did I use. So, I said, there's the tuba right up there, son. He couldn't believe it. He thought, yeah, string bass. Yeah, string bass, see. That's right. What about Saturday Night Function or Double Jack Stomp? Oh, I made all that on the screen. Double Jack Stomp, I wrote that tune. You wrote that tune? Yeah. How'd you get that name? Well, from Amos Nandy. Yeah. Amos Nandy was in Raid that time, so Eldon got that title for it, Double Jack Stomp.
Was that in a movie or something? Did you ever make any movies?

I made a movie. Oh, I made a lot of movies. I was in Bella the 90s with Mae Weston. I was in Earl Carol Vanity, Murder at the Vanity. I was in Black and Tan Fantasy. I was in Backstage. I was... Was it a check and double check movie? That was Amos Nandy in 31. We made that with Amos Nandy. I guess that's how that... Yeah. Yeah. So, he got that title from Amos Nandy, Double Jack Stomp.
